📌 (The guide focuses on real Azure Data Engineering scenarios with ADF, Databricks, Delta Lake & Synapse)

👉 “Explain your end-to-end Azure Data Engineering architecture.”
Most candidates say:
 ❌ “We used ADF and Databricks…”
That’s NOT enough anymore.
💥 What strong candidates explain:
✔️ Source Systems → ADF Pipelines
 ✔️ ADLS Gen2 → Raw Storage

 ✔️ Power BI → Reporting

A retail client processed:
 ✔️ 20M+ transactions daily
 ✔️ Multiple ERP systems
 ✔️ Near real-time dashboards
🚨 Problem?
 Pipeline runtime = 3 HOURS

 ✔️ Delta Lake partitioning
🔥 Result:
 Execution time reduced from 3 hours → 40 minutes
📌 (This exact optimization scenario is explained in the guide)

👉 “ADF vs Databricks?”
Wrong answer:

ai_analysis.summary: This promotional interview-preparation post argues that Azure Data Engineering interviews assess problem-solving and architecture thinking rather than tool familiarity. It presents an end-to-end flow from source systems through ADF, ADLS Gen2, Databricks, Synapse SQL Pool, and Power BI. It also describes a retail scenario processing more than 20 million transactions daily, where parallel ADF activities, Spark optimization, and Delta Lake partitioning reportedly reduced pipeline runtime from three hours to forty minutes. The supplied content does not explain the detailed implementation of those optimizations or include the contents of the linked guides.
subtopics: End-to-end flow from source systems to reporting
Bronze, Silver, and Gold transformation layers

interview_questions.question: How would you walk through the end-to-end Azure Data Engineering architecture described in the post?
interview_questions.answer:
The flow begins with source systems feeding ADF pipelines and then writing to ADLS Gen2 as raw storage.
Databricks handles the Bronze-to-Silver-to-Gold transformations, Synapse SQL Pool supports curated analytics, and Power BI provides reporting.
ADF is framed as the orchestration layer rather than the primary transformation engine.

interview_questions.question: What is the difference between ADF and Databricks in the described architecture?
interview_questions.answer:
ADF is presented as the orchestration layer for pipelines.
Databricks is presented as the layer for large-scale transformations.
The answer should explain that the two technologies can work together rather than treating both as interchangeable ETL tools.

interview_questions.question: A retail pipeline processes more than 20 million transactions daily from multiple ERP systems and has a three-hour runtime. What optimization approach does the post present, and what outcome does it claim?
interview_questions.answer:
The scenario includes multiple ERP sources and near-real-time dashboard requirements.
The proposed changes are parallel activities in ADF, Spark optimization, and Delta Lake partitioning.
The post claims that these changes reduce execution time from three hours to forty minutes.

interview_questions.question: How should a candidate explain an Azure Data Engineering architecture so that the answer demonstrates more than tool familiarity?
interview_questions.answer:
A strong answer states why each technology was selected, what pipeline problem it addressed, and how performance improved.
It connects ADF to orchestration and Databricks to large-scale transformations.
It describes the data flow and claimed performance outcome instead of merely listing tool names.
